title: Biogeochemical Cycles and Ecological Succession
notes: **Carbon cycle:** $CO_2$ fixed by photosynthesis into organic matter, released by respiration, decomposition and combustion. Ocean absorbs and releases $CO_2$. Fossil fuels store ancient carbon.

**Nitrogen cycle:** atmospheric $N_2$ fixed to ammonia by lightning, industrial Haber process, and biological N-fixation (Rhizobium, Azotobacter). Ammonia nitrified to nitrite then nitrate by bacteria. Nitrate assimilated by plants, passed through food chain, returned by denitrification ($NO_3^- \rightarrow N_2$).

**Succession:** gradual replacement of one community by another until a stable climax community is reached. Primary succession starts on bare rock; secondary succession starts on previously colonised soil after disturbance.
**Pioneer species:** first colonisers, usually lichens and mosses, that modify the environment making it suitable for later species.
**Climax community:** stable, self-sustaining community in equilibrium with local climate. In Nepal, temperate forests climax on mid-hills.
